data.title: Backpressure
data.tagline: Backpressure sends a downstream slowdown or pause signal upstream to limit new or unfinished work
data.learningOutcome: You can tell when downstream slowness should feed back upstream and distinguish backpressure from scaling and fixed rate limiting.
data.description: If an image-processing service can finish only a small number of tasks per second while uploads keep arriving, queue length and memory grow without backpressure. The system can slow or pause publishing, or cap unacknowledged work, then resume when capacity recovers. Backpressure is not extra capacity and is not a fixed rate limit independent of downstream state.

learning.assumes: You have seen work pile up, processing slow down, or service memory rise.
learning.outcome: You can tell when downstream slowness should feed back upstream and distinguish backpressure from scaling and fixed rate limiting.

distinctions.label: Rate Limiting
distinctions.explanation: Rate Limit blocks requests exceeding fixed thresholds; Backpressure lets downstream dynamically signal upstream to slow down based on current load.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: When uploads outpace image processing, queue length, unfinished work, and memory rise; when downstream slows or reaches its limit, the system sends that feedback upstream so the producer slows down, pauses, or temporarily stops accepting work.

explanation.title: Judge improvement by recovery evidence
explanation.text: After a simulated peak, queue and memory should stay bounded and publishing should resume when capacity returns. Backpressure does not add capacity or become a fixed rate rule.

explanation.title: Financial report exports also need backpressure
explanation.text: During a bulk report export, data reading may outpace file writing. As the writer nears its capacity limit, it tells the reader to pause and resume after space is available, preventing the export process from exhausting memory as its buffer grows.

data.boundary: Scaling adds processing capacity; fixed rate limiting sets one rate. Backpressure is about downstream state feeding upstream. It does not remove processing failures, so failure and recovery paths still matter.

lessonPractice.title: Image processing is slower than uploads, and queue length and memory are rising. Which change uses backpressure?

options.label: Pause or slow publishing based on downstream capacity, and cap unfinished work
options.feedback: Correct. Backpressure sends the downstream slowdown back upstream and keeps unfinished work bounded.

options.label: Only make the queue larger so more work can accumulate in memory
options.feedback: More capacity delays the symptom but does not tell the upstream that downstream is overloaded.

options.label: Permanently give every user the same fixed rate regardless of downstream state
options.feedback: That is fixed rate limiting, not adapting the flow from downstream feedback.

data.agentPrompt: Add backpressure to the image-processing path: when downstream processing slows or unfinished work reaches its limit, pause or slow the upstream; resume after recovery. Simulate uploads faster than processing and verify that queue and memory do not grow without bound, with trigger and recovery feedback recorded.
